I’ll attach the E2E Long (experimental mode) graphs included in the pull request here for record-keeping.

I drove with WMI model v8 (0e0f6dd2-96dc-4f34-a7cd-63bccc2f5616) for about an hour on the same roads I used to test WMI v7, during a clear daytime drive.

In experimental mode, the E2E longitudinal performance felt very similar to v7, with appropriate and natural acceleration and deceleration. After resetting calibration, the first ~10 minutes showed some ping-pong–like behavior in longitudinal control, but this gradually disappeared after about 10 minutes. It feels like the device is adjusting itself online, which is honestly very impressive technology.

Regarding lateral control, stability has improved compared to v7. It almost feels like v8 includes tuning specifically aimed at improving lateral performance.

I was planning to make WMI v7 my daily driver, but after this drive, I think WMI v8 will be my new daily driver instead.

Explanation for the diagram above:
The thick black lines represent a raised center curb/median.
On roads like this, where the position of the center median has gaps or offsets on the left and right sides, WMI v7 would typically continue straight and then make a late trajectory correction to avoid hitting the curb.
With WMI v8, the behavior is noticeably different. The model appears to anticipate the offset in the center median and select a safer path from the beginning, resulting in a smoother and more confident trajectory without last-moment corrections.
This predictive path selection is the main reason I feel WMI v8 shows a clear lateral performance improvement over v7.
